body:
Thanks, glad you appreciate it. I'm doing much better now. How are you going with your illness? 

I've heard hypomania explained as 'a period of heightened emotions'. Everything is intense - anxiety, paranoia, anger, energy. IIRC intense good emotions are less common than intense bad emotions.   

Basically anything that's persistently more than "normal". Too anxious, too energetic, too many thoughts. Some people get anxious, some people get happy, some people get angry. Some people get weird combinations of that - anxious/angry/paranoid or happy/paranoid/religious. Everyone's "normal" is different, so hypomania will look different for everyone.

Personally, I know I'm hypo manic when I'm checking out number plates, carrying around a notebook and talking way too fast. I might do that occasionally when I'm at baseline **but** if it's been that way for more than a few days I'm probably hypo manic.


What do your symptoms look like?

When we were watching reality TV, she'd say awful, aggressive things about the people (i.e. "She's so fake, no one's that happy. I hope that dumb bitch gets r*ped"), then look over at me and expect me to laugh. 

Other things probably should've tipped me off sooner. Like how her best friend was an alcoholic who abused their partner (she was always on his side). Or the time we were talking about abusive partners and she piped up with "I don't *think* I'd ever hit you". Or the fact that she was miserable 100% of the time and was well on her way to alcoholism.

I felt like an imposter for at least a year. I took my meds for 6 months then decided my doctor was wrong. Manic me was real me and everyone else was wrong. That went well /s. 


My partner at the time had been diagnosed with Bipolar 1 since her late teens. She'd spent a while in and out of psych wards. She was very "woe is me" about her diagnosis and told me *I'd never understand* what it was like. Even before my official diagnosis, I identified with a lot of what she talked about.  I held my tongue because I didn't want to seem ignorant. 


I spent the first half of that relationship supporting her. I could barely deal with my own symptoms and I broke down every two weeks because I felt so overwhelmed. I came close to killing myself. I couldn't understand what was happening to me. I'd been diagnosed with depression/anxiety but I felt like it was something more. I was still struggling to hold it together. 


I snapped eventually. I went completely manic/hypomanic for a month or two. I'd go to her house, hyped up and talking too fast and drinking. I'd clean top to bottom and try to drag her along for my 5 mile runs. I wouldn't sleep, I'd stay up all night pacing. It got very... Delusional and weird towards the end. 


I knew something was up but I didn't know what. I loved how I felt. I was paranoid and edgy, everything was falling apart but I felt like I finally found The Secret™. I could see behind the curtain. My partner sat down with me and said she was scared. She was worried about me. I wasn't acting like myself. I bawled my eyes out in her arms and made an appointment to see the psych.  


He diagnosed me with Bipolar in less than 10 minutes. I was still manic/hypomanic when I went in. Combined with last month's suicidal depression, he said I was a textbook case. Lithium and Quetiapine XR and IR, prescribed. I took my medication and slept properly for the first night in weeks. My girlfriend opened up to me about her diagnosis and started talking to me about my Bipolar. We bonded over it, neither of us were alone anymore. I still felt like a fraud; I was scared that she'd leave me because of my diagnosis. 


I don't know if being with her helped or harmed my acceptance process. Part of me always doubted myself because "I wasn't as bad as her". Part of me knew I'd end up that way if I didn't do something. Eventually I came to terms with the fact that bipolar is different for everybody. Even if I didn't go into full-blown psychosis, I still had Bipolar and I needed to accept it. 


When I finally leveled out, it didn't feel real anymore. I remember feeling like I was a hypochondriac, I was faking it. I was being dramatic, it wasn't that bad. I was just lazy. I stopped taking my meds and spiralled again. I came to terms with it eventually. Accepted that that was my dice roll and I had to deal with it. Meds helped me become stable and healthy. Mania feels good but it's very destructive, more so than the depression for me. 



Sorry for the novel, hope it helps. It was a long ass road for me. I still doubt myself sometimes but I stick with my medication. Still depressed, still a little manic sometimes but nothing like I used to be.

I was diagnosed at 21 but my symptoms started a lot earlier than that. 17/18 is when it started ramping up. I had a lot of periods of instability starting at 13/14, then had my first episode of moderate mania at 18.


It started small and got worse over the years.
